title: The almost-complete hour
hook: A toy task cannot be split. What changes between 39 and 40 available minutes?

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Recognize the discrete completion threshold when a finite time budget must fit indivisible tasks.

misconception: An extra minute can add at most one minute of completed work.
objective: Recognize the discrete completion threshold when a finite time budget must fit indivisible tasks.

claims.text: The named work is The Effective Executive, by Peter F. Drucker, candidate publication year 1967.
claims.source: Peter F. Drucker, The Effective Executive (1967); chapter (unconfirmed); edition and bibliography not independently opened. Access hold F1.

claims.text: The Effective Executive treats recording and consolidating time as a prerequisite for choosing what deserves it.
claims.source: Peter F. Drucker, The Effective Executive (1967); chapter (unconfirmed); edition and bibliography not independently opened. Access hold F1.

claims.text: Original stipulated intervals model: A inputs [39, 20, 0] yield 20; B inputs [40, 20, 0] yield 40. Prediction correct option 40.00. A completes {A} work minutes; B completes {B}. One extra available minute makes a second whole 20-minute task fit instead of leaving 19 unusable minutes. Indivisible toy tasks only; unfinished chunks contribute no output and concentration is not modeled.
claims.source: Original lesson construction; EDD-010 formula ; exact independent Python arithmetic recomputation recorded in answerCheck; no book dataset or measured human response.

claims.text: A toy session has 59 minutes and indivisible 20-minute tasks with no overhead. Completed work minutes? Only two complete tasks fit in 59 minutes, yielding 40 completed work minutes and 19 unused minutes.
claims.source: Original transfer toy, intervals, inputs [59, 20, 0], output 40; independent Python recomputation.
